items.title: ADB lends $75 million to Veritas Finance for MSME credit
points: D Arulmany, Managing Director and CEO, Veritas Finance Pvt Ltd | Photo Credit: N.

RAMAKRISHNAN The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed a $75 million loan agreement with Veritas Finance Limited (VFL) to expand lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in India.
At least 30 per cent of the funds will go to eligible women borrowers.
The ADB financing has also helped mobilize parallel loans of $55 million from commercial lenders.
The project aims to help bridge the MSME financing gap of more than $300 billion and to improve access to formal finance, including for women-owned businesses.
It began operations in 2015 and offers secured business loans, used commercial vehicle loans, affordable home loans and working capital finance.
As of September 2026, its loan portfolio stood at about $1.1 billion, with a presence in more than 500 locations across ten Indian states.

items.title: NaBFID, World Bank Group tie up to channel long-term capital into infrastructure
points: UPLIFT is a joint Partial Credit Enhancement (PCE) facility being developed by NaBFID and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD).
Separately, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) has approved a $1 billion guarantee to mobilise international capital and expand financing for clean energy infrastructure.
The PCE facility aims to deepen the infrastructure bond market by raising issuers’ credit ratings and drawing long-term institutional investors.
The move comes as India targets a $30 trillion economy by 2047, up from $3.9 trillion in FY26.
A NaBFID report estimates the country needs infrastructure investment of about ₹168-172 trillion through FY31, of which only ₹38-40 trillion has been financed so far.

NaBFID Managing Director Rajkiran Rai G said the facility will strengthen bonds as a source of long-term infrastructure finance, while the MIGA guarantee will diversify the institution’s funding sources.
Deputy Managing Director and CFO Monika Kalia said the structure should improve capital efficiency, enable more competitive pricing and expand NaBFID’s capacity to support PCE-backed bond issuances.

items.title: Netherlands opens 2GW offshore wind tender
points: The Netherlands has launched tenders for two offshore wind farms with a combined generating capacity of 2GW, backed by a maximum subsidy budget of nearly €9.5bn ($10.43bn).
The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) opened applications on Thursday for development permits for the IJmuiden Ver Gamma-A and Gamma-B offshore wind sites.
Each site can accommodate a 1GW offshore wind farm, with applications open until December 10.
The maximum subsidy budget has been set at €4.758bn for Gamma-A and €4.698bn for Gamma-B, with maximum tender prices of €117 and €116 per MWh, respectively.

The Dutch government increased the maximum combined subsidy budget from around €7.9bn earlier this year following concerns over rising offshore wind development costs and the planned introduction of charges for using the high-voltage electricity grid.
The tender is being conducted under a temporary offshore wind support mechanism introduced ahead of the Netherlands’ planned adoption of a contract-for-difference system from mid-2027.

items.title: Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026
points: The Union government is set to bring an amended Delimitation Bill that proposes a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, extends the 1971 Census freeze on state seat shares for 25 years and uses the 2011 Census to redraw constituencies within each state.

points: Four boys have been detained for allegedly strangling to death a fellow student of a government residential school in Jharkhand's Chatra district after they were reported to the principal for possessing tobacco products, police said on Friday.
A student of Class 7 at Eklavya Model Residential School in Charu was found dead in his hostel on November 24, with his father alleging that the boy was murdered.
An investigation was initiated, which found that four fellow students, aged between 14 and 16 years, were involved, Chatra Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Sunny Vardhan said.
The victim had reported them to the school principal and hostel warden multiple times, the police officer said.

points: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam.

The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State.

items.title: 34% monsoon deficit, bleak August outlook set alarm bells ringing in Kerala
points: The first two months typically account for around 65% of the total seasonal rainfall.
However, by the end of July, the State had received only 853.8 mm of rainfall against the normal 1,301.7 mm for the period, a deficit of 34%.

Adding to the concern, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast below-normal rainfall for Kerala in August, which typically receives an average of 445.2 mm of rainfall during a normal monsoon, followed by 271.7 mm in September.
This means that only an exceptionally large surplus in August and September could offset the deficit recorded during the peak monsoon months of June and July.
If the latest forecast and prevailing synoptic conditions are any indication, the State appears to be heading towards a drought year, particularly if the monsoon remains weak in August and September.
Global weather models and prevailing synoptic conditions are not favourable for any significant enhancement of rainfall over Kerala during August.

items.title: Keralam may witness early summer-like conditions this year as rain deficit set to widen further

The India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) monthly outlook has forecast below-normal rainfall for September, raising the prospect of the monsoon ending the season with a significant shortfall and paving the way for early summer-like conditions in the State.

Private weather forecasting agency Skymet had earlier downgraded its monsoon forecast for the country to drought, projecting seasonal rainfall at 85% of the Long Period Average (LPA) and putting the probability of a drought at 70%.
Gopal, Director, IMD, Thiruvananthapuram, said Kerala had recorded a 22% rainfall deficit during the first three-fourths of the monsoon season, from June 1 to August 31.

items.title: Keralam Assembly session from Nov 30 to Dec 10; nine bills to be taken up
points: Thiruvananthapuram, Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan on Friday said the third session of the 16th Keralam Legislative Assembly would be held from November 30 to December 10, with nine bills slated for consideration.
The House would sit for nine days, of which eight were earmarked for legislative business and one for non-official members' business, he told reporters.

The bills slated for consideration are the Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Bill, 2026; the Kerala Public Service Commission Amendment Bill, 2026; and the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Bill, 2026.

items.title: Indian Govt's Stupid New Rule Is Making Highway Travel Risky

Rules 138(4)(a) and 95 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989 were amended in October 2020.
The Rule 138 (4) (a) particularly talks about the spare wheel exemption.
Rule 138 governs the mandatory equipment and signals to be carried in motor vehicles.

Amendments also added provisions under Rule 95.

items.title: Indian shares set to open higher, eye fifth weekly gain as inflows boost momentum
points: Indian shares are expected to open higher on Friday as they look to extend their winning run to a fifth straight week, with the unwinding of global AI trade driving a return of foreign flows into local stocks.
GIFT Nifty futures were at 25,962 points, as of 7:51 a.m.
IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index, which closed at 25,884.5 on Thursday.
The 50-stock index and the BSE Sensex are up 0.3% and 0.5%, respectively, so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8% over the last four weeks.

"The (Nifty 50's) ability to hold opening gains, particularly around the psychologically significant 26,000 mark, will be key to sustaining the near-term momentum," said Ponmudi R, CEO at Enrich Money.

items.title: Tata Power: Opportunity or value trap as ambitious growth plans meet execution risks?

items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields Set for Mumbai Debut After $969 Million IPO
points: (Bloomberg) -- Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. , a unit of state-owned Coal India Ltd. , is set to start trading Friday after its initial public offering in the first listing since India’s market regulator barred publishing so-called gray-market prices for IPO…
Indicative pre-listing prices have traditionally served as an informal benchmark for retail and wealthy investors seeking to gauge potential gains on the first day of trading.
Mahanadi Coalfields, which raised 89.81 billion rupees ($969 million) in the offer, will list on the exchanges 114 days after formally kicking off the IPO process on Aug.
5., ranking alongside companies taking the shortest time to go public.

items.title: SC asks HDFC Bank, three others to ok staff prosecution
points: The Supreme Court has ordered HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Housing Finance to grant prosecution sanctions.

Homebuyers were subjected to loan recovery proceedings, even when builders failed to meet their financial obligations.

items.title: JSW Jaecoo J5 Hybrid SUV Spied Undisguised – Debut With Combat On Dec 3?
points: The Jaecoo J5 hybrid SUV has been spotted testing in India without camouflage, revealing its exterior ahead of JSW Motors’ upcoming brand debut.
The SUV is likely to be showcased alongside the Combat on December 3, 2026, although confirmation of the J5’s participation and its India-market name remains awaited.
Latest spy shots, credited to MRD Vlogs, show a black test vehicle carrying Jaecoo lettering, a J5 badge and a clearly visible “HYBRID” badge on the tailgate.
Earlier sightings had established that both electric and ICE-bodied versions of the J5 were undergoing testing in India.
With camouflage removed, the J5’s upright proportions are clearly visible.
The previously reported overseas strong-hybrid setup combines a 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engine with an electric motor and a 1.83 kWh lithium-ion battery.
Quoted combined output is 224 hp and 295 Nm, with rated fuel efficiency of 18.9 km/l.
The J5 would give JSW Motors a more urban-focused midsize SUV alongside the rugged Combat plug-in hybrid.
